title: Critique of lower-margin equations in concrete design codes and of their effect on structural safety software
imageAlt: Size effect plot comparing test data against the ACI-318 code line

narrative.problem: codes like ACI-318 use simplified, lower-margin strength equations that structural safety software then treats as accurate physical probability distributions.
narrative.introduced: a statistical analysis of 784 shear tests showing the code's strength definition sits about 30% below the actual size effect.
narrative.whyItMatters: presented to ACI Committee 445 (Fall 2022) and Committee 348 (Spring 2024), warning that treating code margins as real distributions can mislead safety software.

title: Smooth Lagrangian crack band model with softening spress-sprain relation and crack width prediction
Sprain energy consequences for damage localization and fracture mechanics
imageAlt: Smooth crack band model: sprain energy contour and mesh-sensitivity plots

narrative.problem: classical fracture models treat cracks as lines, causing mesh sensitivity and crack-parallel stress artifacts.
narrative.introduced: a tensorial Lagrange multiplier and a "sprain" concept as a physically motivated localization limiter.

title: Crack-Parallel Stress Effect on Fracture of Fiber-Reinforced Concrete Revealed by Gap Tests
Asymptotically matched extrapolation of fishnet failure probability to continuum scale
venue: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
imageAlt: Discrete-to-continuum transition of fishnet statistics plot

narrative.problem: failure probability behaves differently at small and large scales, with no bridge between them.
narrative.introduced: an asymptotic matching framework, validated against over a million Monte Carlo trials.
narrative.whyItMatters: extrapolates small-scale failure data to continuum-scale risk predictions.
